docs.title: Welcome to the Super Smash Bros. Ultimate Modding Documentation
docs.text:
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate Modding information is scattered everywhere on Discord, Gamebanana, and Github. This website aims to have it all collected into one place so that you can easily find information about Ultimate Modding.

Right now this will most likely just be a list of file formats and programs you can use with them as well as other reverse engineering stuff as that's the only stuff I know about, but hopefully more people will be able to contribute to other stuff.

docs.title: adjb
docs.text:
Renormal mesh adjacency (according to the ssbh_editor github page).

You can use the following program to edit adjb files:

  • ssbh_editor (Windows/MacOS)

You can use the following library to view/modify adjb files:

  • ssbh_lib (Rust)

docs.title: arc
docs.text: There are two types of arc extensions: the data.arc and layout.arc

docs.title: data.arc
docs.text:
The data.arc is the main archive file the game stores all its data in.

You can use the following programs to view and extract from the data.arc:

  • ArcExplorer (Windows/Linux) (Recommended)
  • CrossArc (Windows)

You can use the following library to view/modify the data.arc:

  • smash-arc (Rust)

docs.title: layout.arc
docs.text:
The layout.arc is used to signify how the UI should look.

You can use the following program to modify the layout.arc:

  • Switch Toolbox (Windows)

docs.title: Creating a lopus file
docs.text:
1. Make sure your music file is a WAV file with a sample rate of 48000hz
    • If you're not sure/want to make sure 100% it is, then import your wav into Audacity and set the Project Rate at the bottom left to 48000 then export it to wav
  2. Select two regions in your song and note down the start and end samples if you want your song to loop
  3. Now open up a command prompt instance in the folder with VGAudioCli and run the following command (replace the brackets with the respective information)
    • dotnet VGAudioCli.dll -i <input path> -o <output name>.lopus -l <loop start>-<loop end> --bitrate 64000 --CBR --opusheader namco
  4. Afterwards you should have a lopus file.

docs.title: Using nus3audio-rs
docs.text:
1. Open up a command prompt instance in the folder with the nus3audio program and run the following command (replace the brackets with the respective information)
    • nus3audio -n -A <whatever_you_want> <lopus path> -w <output name>.nus3audio
  2. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Using NUS3Audio Editor
docs.text:
1. Open a pre-existing nus3audio file (either from the data.arc or a pre-existing mod)
  2. Click the first entry in there and press Replace
  3. Select the lopus file
  4. Save the file
  5. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Using simple-nus3audio-gui
docs.text:
1. Click File -> New
  2. Click Edit -> Add Sound
  3. Click the first entry and then Edit -> Sound Properties
  4. Select LOPUS format
  5. Enable Loop Audio
  6. Set Loop from to your start loop sample & Loop to to your loop end sample
  7. Hit Ok
  8. Click Edit -> Replace Single Sound and select your lopus file
  9. Click File -> Save nus3audio and save it
  10. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Using Smash Ultimate Tools
docs.text:
1. Open a pre-existing nus3audio file (either from the data.arc or a pre-existing mod)
  2. Click Choose File on the first entry
  3. Select the lopus file
  4. Save the file
  5. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Creating a idsp file
docs.text:
1. Make sure your music file is a WAV file with any sample rate
    • If you're not sure/want to make sure 100% it is, then import your wav into Audacity and set the Project Rate to anything you want (I recommend 44100hz)
  2. Now open up a command prompt instance in the folder with VGAudioCli and run the following command (replace the brackets with the respective information)
    • dotnet VGAudioCli.dll -i <input path> -o <output name>.idsp
  3. Afterwards you should have a idsp file.

docs.title: Using nus3audio-rs
docs.text:
1. Open up a command prompt instance in the folder with the nus3audio program and run the following command (replace the brackets with the respective information)
    • nus3audio <nus3audio path> -v
  2. Press e and hit enter
  3. Type the id of the entry you want to replace and hit enter
  4. Press d and hit enter
  5. Enter the idsp path you want to replace it with and hit enter
  6. Press q and hit enter
  7. Repeat 2-6 for each entry you want to edit
  8. Press w and hit enter
  9. Enter <nus3audio name>.nus3audio and hit enter
  10. Press q and hit enter
  11. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Using NUS3Audio Editor
docs.text:
1. Open the nus3audio file you want to edit
  2. Click the entry you want to replace and press Replace
  3. Select the idsp file you want to replace it with
  4. Repeat 2-3 for each entry you want to edit
  5. Save the file
  6. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Using simple-nus3audio-gui
docs.text:
1. Open the nus3audio file you want to edit
  2. Select the entry you want to edit
  3. Click Edit -> Replace Single Sound or press Ctrl + R
  4. Select the idsp file you want to replace it with
  5. Repeat 2-4 for each entry you want to edit
  6. Save the file
  7. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Using Smash Ultimate Tools
docs.text:
1. Open the nus3audio file you want to edit
  2. Click Choose File for the entry you want to edit
  3. Select the idsp file you want to replace it with
  4. Repeat 2-3 for each entry you want to edit
  5. Save the file
  6. You're now done with the nus3audio. Move on to Loading the nus3audio in-game

docs.title: Loading the nus3audio in-game
docs.text:
1. Make sure you have ARCropolis set up properly and working
  2. Create a folder in sd:/ultimate/mods with any folder name (I recommend naming it something related to what the mod does)
  3. Inside that folder, replicate the ARC path of the file you want to replace (make sure you replace : with ;)
  4. Launch the game and make sure the mod is enabled and it should work!
Format: sd:/ultimate/mods/<Mod Folder Name>/<ARC path>
Examples:
sd:/ultimate/mods/My Cool Music Mods/stream;/sound/bgm/bgm_crs01_menu.nus3audio
sd:/ultimate/mods/Super Cool Sonic Voice Mod/sound/bank/fighter_voice/vc_sonic.nus3audio

docs.title: Dumping with a Hacked Switch
docs.text:
1. Open up the Homebrew Launcher and launch nxdumptool
    • If you're using a gamecard, then select the Dump Gamecard option
    • If you downloaded the game digitally, then select Dump installed SD card / eMMC content and select Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
  2. Select the RomFS options
  3. Set Use update/DLC to the latest update version (currently v1769472)
  4. Press RomFS section data dump and wait for the game to dump
  5. Shut down your switch and insert your SD Card into your computer
  6. Navigate to sd:/switch/nxdumptool/RomFS
    • If your SD Card is FAT32, delete the .nrr folder in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate <Update Number> (01006A800016E800) (UPD) then go back to the RomFS folder and open up command prompt in that folder and run the following command (replace <Update Number> with the update number and <output dir> with where you want to save the data.arc locally) copy /b "Super Smash Bros. Ultimate <Update Number> (01006A800016E800) (UPD)\*" "<output dir>\data.arc"
    • If your SD Card is exFAT, then just copy the data.arc in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate <Update Number> (01006A800016E800) (UPD) somewhere to your PC
  8. Remove the dump on your sd card
  9. You're done

docs.title: Dumping with Ryujinx
docs.text:
1. Right-click on Super Smash Bros. Ultimate game and select Manage Title Updates
  2. Make sure the latest update is selected and click Ok
  3. Right-click on Super Smash Bros. Ultimate and click Extract Data -> RomFS
  4. Wait for Ryujinx to finish dumping Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
  5. You're done

docs.title: Dumping with Yuzu
docs.text:
1. Right-click on Super Smash Bros. Ultimate game and select Properties
  2. Make sure the latest update is checked and click OK
  3. Right-click on Super Smash Bros. Ultimate and click Dump RomFS -> Dump RomFS
  4. Wait for Yuzu to finish dumping Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
  5. You're done

docs.title: Modding Setup
docs.text:
To run our mods and custom code, we either need to modify the console to run a custom firmware or use Ryujinx. For the console, we'll be using Atmosphere for this, since it's the most stable custom firmware and the only one being actively worked on.

Covering how to mod your switch from scratch would be a undertaking that this site isn't suited for, so follow this guide here to setup Atmosphere on your switch.

This guide will be a minimal guide to getting the barebones of Super Smash Bros. Ultimate Modding set up. If you want a more comprehensive guide for just using mods, you can follow this guide for console modding or follow this guide for Ryujinx modding.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text:
• If a folder doesn't exist, then create it
  • If it asks you to overwrite, then overwrite
  • sd:/ means the root of your SD Card (like the C:/ drive or D:/ drive)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Skyline (Switch/Ryujinx)
  • ARCropolis (Switch/Ryujinx)
  • sys-ftpd-light (Switch)
  • One of the FTP clients (Console Only)
    • FileZilla (Switch) (Windows/MacOS/Linux)

docs.title: Setting up the SD Card
docs.text:
1. Copy the exefs folder in the Skyline download to sd:/atmosphere/contents/01006A800016E000/
  2. Copy the atmosphere & ultimate folders in the ARCropolis download to sd:/
  3. Copy the atmosphere & config folders in the sys-ftpd-light download to sd:/
  4. Boot into Atmosphere and open up Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
  5. Check the update title at the top left of the title screen. If it says ARCropolis Ver. X.X.X, then you're done!

docs.title: Using FTP to access and modify your SD Card over Network
docs.text:
1. Install FileZilla (following the installer on-screen instructions (make sure to not install the ads in the installer!))
  2. Open up FileZilla
  3. In the following fields, enter the following information:
    • Host -> your switch's IP address
    • Port -> 5000
  4. Click Quickconnect and then click OK on the pop-up
  5. You should now be successfully connected to your switch! Now you can transfer files over the network without having to take out the microSD card.

docs.title: Ryujinx Setup
docs.text:
1. Right-click on Super Smash Bros. Ultimate in Ryujinx and click Open Mods Directory
  2. Copy the exefs folder in the Skyline download to the directory that was opened by Ryujinx
  3. Navigate to atmosphere/contents/01006A800016E000/ in the ARCropolis zip and copy the romfs folder to the directory that was opened by Ryujinx
  4. Run Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
  5. Check the update title at the top left of the title screen. If it says ARCropolis Ver. X.X.X, then you're done!

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text: This guide will only cover GDB will for the switch console itself! If you want to set up GDB using an emulator, you can follow this guide on Luminescent Platinum documentation.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Debian WSL (Windows)
  • Custom .gdbinit

docs.title: Setting up on the Switch side
docs.text:
1. Make sure you have the latest Atmosphere set up and running!
  2. Edit sd:/atmosphere/config/system_settings.ini (or create it if it's not there) and paste the following in (reboot the switch after you save the file):
[atmosphere]
enable_htc = u8!0x0
enable_standalone_gdbstub = u8!0x1

docs.title: Setting up WSL (Windows Only)
docs.text:
1. Download Debian from the Microsoft Store
  2. Once it's done, run the Debian application
  3. If you run into The Windows Subsystem for Linux optional component is not enabled, then search for Windows Features, then scroll down and enable Windows Subsystem for Linux
  4. Set a password and confirm

docs.title: Setting up GDB
docs.text:
1. Run sudo apt-get -y update && sudo apt-get -y install gdb-multiarch && sudo apt-get -y install wget (this will update your repos, install gdb-multiarch, and install wget)
  2. Run wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Coolsonickirby/smash-ultimate-research-setup/main/gdbinit/.gdbinit -O ~/.gdbinit && wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Coolsonickirby/smash-ultimate-research-setup/main/gdbinit/attach.py -O ~/attach.py && wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Coolsonickirby/smash-ultimate-research-setup/main/gdbinit/.gdbinit.switch -O ~/.gdbinit.switch && wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Coolsonickirby/smash-ultimate-research-setup/main/gdbinit/print_addr_setup.py -O ~/print_addr_setup.py (this will download and set up the custom .gdbinit, .gdbinit.switch, attach.py, and print_addr_setup.py files for convenience)
  3. Run nano ~/.gdbinit.switch and scroll down until you get to the target extended-remote line
  4. Edit the IP in the file to be your switch's IP (you can find the switch's IP by going to System Settings -> Internet -> IP Address)
  5. Hit Ctrl + X -> Y -> Enter
  6. You're done, GDB is now set up with auto-attach + a handful of useful functions!

docs.title: Using GDB
docs.text:
1. Open up Debian if you're on Windows
  2. Run gdb-multiarch
  3. Run Super Smash Bros. Ultimate on the switch once it says to "Launch your game"
  4. Let it auto-attach and set $main automatically
  5. Set up any breakpoints, no_ops, stubs, etc...
  6. Type c and hit enter

docs.title: GDB Functions
docs.text:
The .gdbinit file we set up earlier has these handful of functions that will be pretty useful in your reversing endeavors!

  • my_bt -> Prints the backtrace as absolute addresses. Often misses the first address on the backtrace but you can just p/x $lr for that.
  • my_bt2 -> Prints the backtrace with offsets relative to the base of main.
  • no_op <offset> -> Takes an offset into main and NOPs the instruction at that address
  • stub <offset> -> Takes an offset into main and stubs the function at that address
  • replace <offset> <new_instruction> -> Replaces the instruction at an offset with the new instruction
  • get_pc -> Gets the PC as an offset relative to the base of main
  • break_at <offset> -> Sets a breakpoint at an offset relative to the base of main
  • localize <register/address> -> Converts the value in the register (or the passed address) to an offset relative to the base of main
  • xxd <address> <size> -> Print a xxd dump of the address
  • print_trace -> Runs get_pc, localize $lr, & my_bt2 to get the current offset, the calling offset, and the backtrace in one command instead of three

docs.title: Disabling Auto-Play on Playlist Music Selection
Disabling Auto-Play on Playlist Music Selection
docs.text: This walkthrough will explain the process of using the shared Smash Ultimate Research Server to disable and prevent the music from being played after selecting a track in the normal playlist menu.

docs.title: Things we'll cover
docs.text:
• Using Ghidra and the shared Smash Ultimate Research Server to find useful functions
  • Using GDB to break at said functions and view backtraces
  • Track down the instruction which calls the function to play the music after selecting it
  • noping said instruction to prevent the song from playing after selecting it
  • Creating a skyline plugin with our research to automatically perform the patch for us

Let's get started!

docs.title: The start
docs.text:
So first things first, lets go ahead and open up the main decompiled code in Ghidra from the shared Smash Ultimate Research Server.

Let's go ahead and search in the symbol tree for anything that might be related to music and see if we get any hits. I'll use bgm since that's something commonly associated with music.

Hooo boy! That's a lotta stuff! Luckily for us though, we can ignore everything in the Exports since those are only accessed by the lua files. We have some functions with the label FUN_, so we'll ignore all of those until we're desperate. There are some functions inside namespaces, which from my expierence don't matter much. There are also a couple of labels, but those are for the game's reference. So now we're left with the following functions:

  • bgm_related
  • get_bgm_save_no
  • get_ui_bgm_entry_idx_by_id
  • play_bgm_by_prc_entry_index

bgm_related and get_bgm_save_no are out of it for me, since the first one is still not exactly known while the other is clearly known for something unrelated to our mission. So now we only have two.

I'll personally decide to go with play_bgm_by_prc_entry_index, since that function sounds like it's in charge of playing the bgms.

Now that we decided on the function, we'll need to get it's offset. To do so, we'll click on the function in the Symbol Tree and look at the first offset after the function declaration. As we can see here, the offset is 71033135f0. However, we need to remove the 710 prefix and put a 0x prefix instead because 710 is the base address in Ghidra. So the offset we'll use in Rust and GDB will be 0x33135f0

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
We have our offset, so now we can start having the real fun 😈! We'll go ahead and start GDB in Debian and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate on the switch. Once GDB attaches and finds main, we can run break_at 0x33135f0 to set a breakpoint at the function we found. That means everytime that function runs, the game will pause and we can see what's going on in memory.

Let's go ahead and enter c, then get to the Stage Selection Screen and open up a playlist. When we trying playing a song with the Y button, the game freezes! Don't worry though, your game didn't crash. GDB stopped the game and now you can run commands in GDB.

We can enter our commands into GDB, we'll run the print_trace command to get the current $pc (pc being the current offset we're at in the code), the $lr (lr being the instruction that we'll jump back to after our function is over), and the backtrace (a list keeping track of which offset to jump back to).

Keeping a note of this output in case we need to compare it to another scenario will be extremely helpful the more deeper you dive into reversing.

We'll continue (type c and hit enter) and try to select a song by choosing it this time. When we press A to choose the game, the game freezes again! Just like before, the function got called, so let's go ahead and run the print_trace command again.

Oho? What's this? The second offset in the chosen song playback is different than the second offset in the manually chosen playback. This means that if we modify anything in the first offset, then it'll affect both, manually playing the song and the game automatically playing the song. That's pretty interesting. Let's go ahead and jump to the second offset in the chosen song playback in Ghidra since that's what we want to prevent.

docs.title: Tracking
docs.text:
We can press g in Ghidra to jump to an offset. Although when we jump to an offset, we need to add 710 before the offset, since Ghidra starts at 710 (so in our case, we'll be jumping to 7101b352ac in Ghidra) (Please ignore the horrible hard to read text on the right, that's just a side-effect with the Dark Mode Ghidra theme lol)

If we look closely, we can see that we landed at the instruction right after a bl (branch link), which is how aarch64 calls functions. If we double click the function, we can see that it calls play_bgm_by_prc_entry_index in it

docs.title: Noping
docs.text:
So now that we know that function calls another function that runs the play_bgm_by_prc_entry_index, lets change the bl instruction to a nop. Since I didn't explain it earlier, a nop is a instruction that does absolutely nothing, and that's what makes it special. So let's say that we don't want the bl instruction to jump to a different function. All we need to do is replace the bl instruction with a nop instruction and mission accomplished! To replace the instruction with a nop, we just need to copy the offset of the bl instruction (7101b352a8 -> 0x1b352a8) and use the no_op function we have in GDB. (If you accidentally continued, then you can freeze the game at any moment by pressing Ctrl + C)

Now whenever the game hits the code to jump to the other function, instead it'll see a nop, then it'll think it has to do nothing and keep going, which means the function to play the music will be skipped. Let's continue the game and see what happens when we try playing a song.

Success! Congratulations! You have successfully reversed and patched the game to not auto-play the music on selection in the playlist menu!

docs.title: Converting into a Skyline Plugin
docs.text:
We have our newfound knowledge on how to prevent the game from automatically playing the music when we pick a song, but now we have to manually no_op the function every time we want the game to not play the song. If we want to distribute this as a mod so that users can enjoy it, we can't expect them to have GDB and be willing to put up with manually noping the instruction themselves every time. That's where skyline plugins come in! We'll create a sklyine plugin that patches the offset with a nop instruction every time the game boots!

So first, we'll run the cargo skyline new <project_name> command to make a new skyline project. Then open up that folder with your favorite IDE (I'll be using VSCode).

Go to src/lib.rs and remove the println!(...) line from the main function. Now make a new line in main() and write the following: skyline::patching::Patch::in_text(0x1b352a8).nop().expect("Failed to patch 0x1b352a8") This line basically says "Hey, go to the .text section (where the code is stored), then jump to the offset given (0x1b352a8, which is what we noped), then nop. If you fail to nop it, then throw an error message!". Now we can run cargo skyline run and test it out in-game!

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: I'd say we cleared all of our goals in this walkthrough! We used the Shared Research Server to track down a promising function, used GDB to break and inspect the stack trace, tracked down the instruction which jumped to the function that called the play_bgm function, noped said instruction, and converted it to a skyline plugin.

docs.title: Automatically adding new characall files

Instead of manually adding new entries to the nus3bank and soundlabelinfo for new announcer character calls, The CSK Collection scans all files in mods:/sound/bank/narration, and if it's a new file, then it automatically adds it to the nus3audio, nus3bank, and soundlabelinfo so that those new files can be accessed by the game.

docs.title: Custom Palutena Guidances
docs.text:
The CSK Collection changes how Palutena Guidance works, allowing for new guidances to be created and associated with a Character ID instead of a Fighter Kind. You can read more on this page to learn how to create your own guidance.

Note: mod:/ in this guide refers to your custom mod folder.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: • A wav file containing all the dialouge with a sample rate of 48khz (if you're unsure of how to change the sample rate, then please refer to the Music Modding guide)

docs.title: Optional
docs.text:
• Example wav file
  • Example json file (you can use Load Config to load the file and interact with it in the editor)

docs.title: Creating the Guidance
docs.text:
1. Navigate to PaluGuide

  2. Enter the following information in the respective boxes at the lower left:

    • ui_chara_id -> The Character ID you want to set the guidance for
    • pattern -> The cXX index you want this guidance to target
    • name_id -> The name_id of the Character ID

  3. Press Load Audio File on the bottom right side and select the wav from earlier

  4. Add the amount of regions you desire (usually one for each character that speaks)

  5. Move and resize each region by dragging either the center of it around or dragging the left/right edge of it inward/outward respectively.

  6. Select each region in the Regions section, then fill out the following information:

    • Event Start (will run when entering the region):
      • Left -> The portrait that will appear on the left side
      • Left (Outside) -> The portrait that will appear on the left side closer to the screen's edge
      • Right -> The portrait that will appear on the right side
      • Right (Outside) -> The portrait that will appear on the right side closer to the screen's edge
      • Text Delay -> The amount of frames the text will be delayed from showing up
    • Event End (will run when leaving the region):
      • Slide Left Out -> Will slide the portraits on the left out of the screen
      • Slide Right Out -> Will slide the portraits on the right out of the screen
    • Text -> The text that will show up

  7. Select the first region in the Regions section and press Toggle to preview your custom guidance

  8. Once you're ready, press Save and save the generated file

docs.title: Preparing the guidance for in-game
docs.text:
1. In your mod folder, create the following path: mod:/smashappeal/palutena/data

  2. Place the generated file in that folder

  3. Convert your wav file to a nus3audio. You can use the following (Make sure looping is disabled!):

    • Music Modding guide
    • SmashUltimateTools

  4. Rename your nus3audio to the following: vc_smashappeal_angeland_<name_id>.nus3audio, where <name_id> is the name_id you used earlier

  5. Create the following path: mod:/stream;/sound/smashappeal

  6. Place your nus3audio file in that folder

  7. Test it out in game!

docs.title: Native Color Redirection
docs.text:
To redirect colors natively in-game, create a file called mods:/flags/reslot.toml in your mod folder, then use the following config as a base:

[chara_id]
c<Source Color> = <Target Color>

Where <Source Color> amd <Target Color> are numbers (limited from 0 to 255.)

An example of a proper config would look something like this:

[pichu]
c00 = 6
c06 = 0

[sonic]
c00 = 2

In this example, Pichu's flower color and the default color swap places, and Sonic's default color is set to the light blue skin. You can add as many character entries as you want.

docs.title: One Slot Series
docs.text:
Warning: This feature is very unstable and will crash the game if it's not used in Smash mode 1v1 only.

To use the One Slot Series feature, create a flag called mods:/flags/enable_one_slot_series.flag, then add a new key to the character database entry in ui_chara_db.prc with the type of Hash40 and a key of ui_series_id_cXX (replace cXX with the color you want to set), then set the value to be the ui_series_id you want to set it to.

docs.title: Play Music on CSS
docs.text:
This feature will specifically play music on the Character Selection Screen, and will revert back to the menu track when going back to the Stage Selection Screen.

To enable this feature, create a file called mods:/flags/play_music_on_css.flag. After creating the file, open it up with any text editor, then add a ui_bgm_id per line to select which tracks can be picked for the CSS Menu Music.

An example file would be as such:

ui_bgm_a67_sm64_slider
ui_bgm_w02_sm64_rainbowcruise

This will pick either Slide or Slide (Remix) to play in the CSS. To get the list of tracks and their respective filenames, you can use this site. Just make sure to add ui_ to the filename when adding it to the flag.

docs.title: Randomize Announcer Clips
docs.text: This feature allows you to randomize the announcer clips. To use it, simply create a folder mods:/random-tones/<My Own Folder> (where <My Own Folder> can be named any legal path), then place your custom nus3audio announcer in there.

docs.title: Restore Announcer First, Fighter Name Last for Victory ("The Winner Is...")
Restore Announcer First, Fighter Name Last for Victory ("The Winner Is...")
docs.text:
This feature restores the announcer starting with "The Winner Is..." followed by the winner's name.

To enable this feature, create a file called mods:/flags/the_winner_is.flag.

It's recommended to use the pre-made Restore The Winner Is folder that comes with the CSK Collection.

docs.title: Show Music Track on Pause
docs.text:
Important Note: By default, the Music Track info overlays with the "PAUSE" text. The CSK Collection comes with a info_melee/layout.arc modified to account for this, and it's recommended that you use this if you plan on using this feature. If this conflicts with another mod that also modifies this file, then you can delete the one that comes with the CSK Collection and manually move the track container down.

This feature will show what track is currently playing when you pause during a match.

To enable this feature, create a file called mods:/flags/show_track_on_pause.flag.

It's recommended to use the pre-made Show Music Track on Pause folder that comes with the CSK Collection.

docs.title: Stage Redirection
docs.text:
By default, this feature is disabled. If you want to enable this feature, then create a file called mods:/flags/enable_stage_redirection.flag.

Stage Redirection allows you to create a new entry in the stage database, then linking the set stage_place_id and the ui_stage_id to a custom stage resource entry.

docs.title: Unique Results Stage
docs.text: This feature lets you set a unique results stage for either a color, a victory animation, or both.

docs.title: Unique Victory Animation Results Stage
docs.text:
To set a stage for a specific victory animation, create the flag mods:/camera/fighter/<Fighter Codename>/c<XX>/j02win<Y>.stage, where:

  • <Fighter Codename> -> The fighter's internal name used by the game

  • <XX> -> The targeted color

  • <Y> -> The targeted animation

Once created, open up the file in any text editor and insert the stage's dir info you want to use. A list can be found at the bottom of this page.

docs.title: Unique Fighter Color Results Stage
docs.text:
To set a stage for a specific fighter's color in general, create the flag mods:/fighter/<Fighter Codename>/model/body/c<XX>/result.stage, where:

  • <Fighter Codename> -> The fighter's internal name used by the game

  • <XX> -> The targeted color

Once created, open up the file in any text editor and insert the stage's dir info you want to use. A list can be found at the bottom of this page.

docs.title: Unique Fighter Results Stage
docs.text:
Warning: Any cloned fighter will use the original's results stage as well if you use this method.

To set a stage for a specific fighter in general, create the flag mods:/fighter/<Fighter Codename>/result.stage, where:

  • <Fighter Codename> -> The fighter's internal name used by the game

Once created, open up the file in any text editor and insert the stage's dir info you want to use. A list can be found at the bottom of this page.

docs.title: Unique Victory Animation Kime Frame Value
Unique Victory Animation Kime Frame Value
docs.text:
The "Kime Frame" refers to the intense splash after the character that won performs their victory animation.

The red and white splash screen that shows up after Sonic pumps his fist is the "Kime"

By default, for all animations it's set to happen at frame 130. You can customize this by creating a file at camera/fighter/<Fighter Name>/<cXX>/j02win<Y>.kime, where:

  • <Fighter Name> -> The fighter's codename
  • <cXX> -> The color you want to set the kime frame for
  • <Y> -> The victory animation you want to change the kime frame for

Once you created the file, open it up in Notepad (or any text editor) and enter the frame you want the Kime to happen at, then save it.

docs.title: Unlock All BGM Tracks
docs.text:
This feature makes it so that all entries in BGM Database are unlocked.

To enable this feature, create a file called mods:/flags/unlock_all_bgm.flag.

docs.title: Unlock All Characters
docs.text:
This feature makes it so that all characters will be avaliable to be chosen in the Smash Menu, however, you will still get the unlock challenge for fighters.

To enable this feature, create a file called mods:/flags/unlock_all_fighters.flag.

If you want the fighters to be unlocked properly, then its better to use this plugin made by asimon-1/CPU_1. This plugin runs by itself and unlocks all the characters legitimately for you. Make sure to read its README properly before using it.

docs.title: Unlock Final Smash, Special Hit, and Assist Camera
Unlock Final Smash, Special Hit, and Assist Camera
docs.text:
Normally, when you use a Final Smash, land a special hit (ex. Deadly Hit), or have an assist on the field, the Camera option is disabled to prevent issues that can occur. This feature removes that restriction and allows you to use it (though you can encounter issues.)

Used alongside the Unrestircted Camera mod

To enable this feature, create a file called mods:/flags/unlock_camera.flag.

It's recommended that when using this feature, you use the Unrestircted Camera mod created by ThatNintendoNerd/TNN, as some Final Smashes happen where the controllable camera can't move to.

docs.title: Unshared Final Smash Movies
docs.text:
To use this feature, place the movie file you have prepared in prebuilt:/movie/fighter/<Fighter Name>/<cXX>/<Movie File>, where:

  • <Fighter Name> -> The fighter's codename
  • <cXX> -> The color you want the movie to be for
  • <Movie File> -> Usually named final_00.h264, with Joker having an extra one called final_01.h264 for the alternate All-Out Attack

docs.title: Important!
docs.text: Most final smash movies that are on GameBanana come with a config.json that adds an unshare-blacklist key. While this does fix it not loading normally, it messes with this feature. To fix this, just open up the config.json and remove the unshare-blacklist key and array.

docs.title: Unshared "Kazuya Wins" Announcer
docs.text: By default, the "Kazuya Wins" announcer voice cannot be one slotted. However, thanks to Zarek, it now can! Make sure to use the files that are in Kazuya One Slot Announcer.

docs.title: Unshared Victory Cameras
docs.text:
To use this feature, simply place your custom victory camera file at camera/fighter/<Fighter Name>/<cXX>, where:

  • <Fighter Name> -> The fighter's codename
  • <cXX> -> The color you want to replace the victory camera for

docs.title: Victory Themes Features
docs.text:
It's recommended to use this unshared victory theme mod so options don't apply to characters that share the same victory theme file.

The features related to the victory theme are conglomerated to this page. You can get the list of all victory themes from here (make sure to click More Options and select Victory Themes)

docs.title: Color Specific Victory Themes (formerly known as "One Slot Victory Themes")
docs.text:
To set a victory theme for a specific color, you can simply rename your custom victory theme file to <original_victory_filename>_c<XX>.nus3audio (where <XX> is the color you want to set) and place it in stream;/sound/bgm.

Examples:

  • bgm_z47_f_sonic_c02.nus3audio -> Changes Sonic's third color victory theme

  • bgm_z01_f_mario_c00.nus3audio -> Changes Mario's first color victory theme

  • bgm_z46_f_snake_c04.nus3audio -> Changes Snake's fifth color victory theme

docs.title: Unique Victory Animation Victory Theme
docs.text:
To set a victory theme for a specific victory animation, you can simply rename your custom victory theme file to <original_victory_filename>_j02win<X>.nus3audio (where <X> is the victory animation number) and place it in stream;/sound/bgm.

Examples:

  • bgm_z47_f_sonic_j02win2.nus3audio -> Changes Sonic running and grabbing the Chaos Emerald animation victory theme

  • bgm_z99_f_buddy_j02win1.nus3audio -> Changes Banjo throwing a Jiggy into the air, catching it, then giving a thumbs up animation victory theme

docs.title: Combining both of these
docs.text:
You can combine both of these features to set a victory theme for a specific animation if the character is on a specific color. To do so, simply rename your custom victory theme file to <original_victory_filename>_j02win<Y>_c<XX>.nus3audio (where <Y> is the victory animation number and <XX> is the color you want to set) and place it in stream;/sound/bgm.

Example:

  • bgm_z16_f_iceclimber_j02win2_c01.nus3audio -> Changes Ice Climbers second color nodding and high fiving animation victory theme

docs.title: Using a configuration file
docs.text:
While the older way of using this feature was limited to a configuration file, this is now left as an option for those who still want to use it. To use a configuration file, simply create a file in mods:/osvt/<Config File>.toml (where <Config File> is any legal filename.)

The structure of the configuration is as follows:

[<bgm_filename>]
c<XX> = <value>
j02win<Y> = <value>
j02win<Y>_c<XX> = <value>

where:

  • <bgm_filename> -> The filename of the victory theme

  • <XX> -> The color you want to target

  • <Y> -> The victory animation you want to target

  • <value> -> Either the index to use from the victory file, or a string to another victory filename to use

An example of a configuration file is provided here:

[bgm_z47_f_sonic]
c01 = "bgm_u09_sadv2_liveandlearn"
c02 = "bgm_z01_f_mario"
j02win2 = 1
j02win2_c02 = "bgm_u12_snc06_hisworld_instrumental"

[bgm_z01_f_mario]
c00 = "bgm_z47_f_sonic"
c01 = "bgm_a04_lnd_chika"

This configuration will do the following:

[bgm_z47_f_sonic]:

  • c01 -> Cause Sonic's second color to play Live and Learn if the victory animation isn't the second one

  • c02 -> Cause Sonic's third color to play Mario's victory theme if the animation isn't the second one

  • j02win2 -> Cause the "grabbing Chaos Emerald" animation to play the first index in Sonic's victory theme file

  • j02win2_c02 -> Cause the "grabbing Chaos Emerald" animation to play "His World" IF Sonic is set to the third color

[bgm_z01_f_mario]:

  • c00 -> Cause Mario's first color to play Sonic's victory theme

  • c01 -> Cause Mario's second color to play "Underground Theme - Super Mario Land (Remix)"

docs.title: What is the CSK Collection
docs.text:
Latest Version: 6.0.0 (13.0.5)

This is a plugin containing multiple features, some that activate automatically and others that rely on flags. It also contains API calls that other plugins can use.

Notice: When mods:/ is used anywhere in the following pages, this refers to any mod folder in sd:/ultimate/mods. It can either be a mod folder you created yourself or a mod that already exists within it.
